esdi_renormalization_note: The headline ESDI renormalises the covered sectors (their weights sum to less than 1 because gas and coal are uncovered). esdi_all_sectors is the same figure with gas and coal counted as present-at-zero; the gap is the uplift that excluding them adds. Gas is not unmeasured -- it carries documented strikes that score zero for want of a defensible denominator.

transmission_concentration.note: Transmission is an event-burden measure against a saturation constant (8), so it is dominated by the freshest strikes in a thin sector -- currently the Kerch power bridge (Taman) and occupied-Crimea substations, not the wider Russian grid. Read it as theatre-concentrated, not national.

transmission_sensitivity.note: Transmission is an event-burden against a saturation constant, not a national-grid capacity measure. It is dominated by 1-2 theatres and the headline value roughly halves/doubles as the saturation constant moves between 16 and 4. Published as a sensitivity, not a tuning knob.
transmission_sensitivity.red_team_verdict: RETAINED in the headline. It reflects real, sourced disruption to the Kerch power bridge and Crimea substations; removing it would discard that signal and would amount to tuning away an inconvenient theatre. It is retained WITH mandatory concentration disclosure and these alternatives, and is NOT presented as national grid exposure. Flagged for the independent red-team.

assessed_degradation.note: Assessed degradation counts only capacity a source explicitly quantified. It is deliberately distinct from exposure, which counts capacity at disrupted sites regardless of measured loss.

recovery_stats.note: Recovery is tracked per incident and counted by DISTINCT EPISODE: a multi-day strike counts once. National observed-restoration evidence is n=7. A per-CLASS median appears only where a class has >= 3 independent observed episodes; the pooled cross-class figure is MIXED-INFRASTRUCTURE evidence, not a generic repair time, and is never the headline. 'modelled' scoring means no credible source-reported timing exists; a partial restart (including flow rerouted around a still-damaged node) is recorded but never treated as full reconstitution.

coverage_detail.note: Counts of enumerated events only. A low count may mean genuinely low disruption OR thin open-source reporting for that bucket; this dataset cannot always distinguish the two, and does not pretend to.

gas_processing.caveat: Within-census share only. The census is a non-exhaustive, bottom-up sample of publicly-sourced gas-processing capacities (bcm/y raw gas) — NOT a national denominator — so this is not national gas-processing exposure. Experimental: excluded from the headline ESDI pending an independent red-team.

estimate_days.basis: Orenburg Governor Yevgeny Solntsev: the Orsknefteorgsintez primary refining unit was fully shut after the 10-11 Aug 2026 strike; because the damaged equipment is imported and under sanctions, repairs could take UP TO six months. Encoded as a 120-180 day band (central 150) with 180 as the stated ceiling.

recovery.what_source_establishes: Orsk refinery fully shut down after the 10-11 Aug 2026 drone strike damaged its primary refining unit; the Orenburg governor publicly estimated repairs could take up to six months owing to sanctioned imported equipment. An estimate with no confirmed restart as of the as-of date.

After the 20 Aug 2026 strike on the 500 kV Taman substation (through which all four Kerch energy-bridge lines pass), the Russian-installed head of Sevastopol said power restrictions in the affected Crimean cities were lifted after ~90 minutes but the grid remained unstable. This is emergency-switching restoration of supply, NOT confirmed repair of the damaged substation; renewed Crimea outages the next night are consistent with the hub not being reconstituted. observed_days left blank: the node itself was not restored.
Interfax: by early July 2026 the plant was accepting only ~28% of normal Karachaganak gas, with no timeline for full resumption - a partial restart, not full reconstitution.

estimate_days.basis: Industry source cited by Reuters: repairs to the damaged CDU-10 (~38% of plant capacity) would take at least half a year

recovery.what_source_establishes: Reuters industry source estimated Omsk's damaged CDU-10 would take at least half a year to repair. A credible sourced estimate (medium confidence): its central value drives the modelled horizon for this incident. No restart reported as of the as-of date.

estimate_days.basis: Aggregated industry sources via the Wikipedia strike table expected the refinery offline at least 6 months after the June 2026 strikes

recovery.what_source_establishes: Aggregated, indirect sourcing expected the Moscow Refinery offline at least 6 months after the June 2026 strikes. LOW confidence: the estimate is displayed but is NOT used to drive the decay curve, which falls back to the modelled sector horizon.

recovery.what_source_establishes: Reuters/Rigzone reporting tied to the next (31 July 2026) strike states the LUKOIL Volgograd refinery had only recently restored throughput, nearly recovering its runs to levels seen before earlier strikes, a lull having let drone-hit refineries complete repairs. Confirms substantial recovery of runs after the late-May/early-June strike, before 31 July; no exact restart date given (observed_days blank).

Following the 21 July 2026 strikes on the Zorya, Morske and Gaspra substations, the 110 kV Gaspra substation was hit and power was briefly lost before being partially restored; operator Krymenergo said the Gaspra facility was undergoing major reconstruction. A same-night partial re-energisation of supply while the struck node stayed out of service / under reconstruction. observed_days left blank: supply, not the substation, was restored.

recovery.what_source_establishes: Reuters industry sources: Rosneft's Kuibyshev refinery (struck 9-10 June 2026, one episode) resumed operations on 21 August 2026 after major repairs that began 1 July -- ~72 days after the disruption. Establishes a restart to operation, not proven full-capacity reconstitution. A further 28 Aug 2026 strike is after this dataset's as-of date.

Reuters/Izvestia: the plant resumed and power/water were functioning by 24 Nov 2025, heat maintained via mobile modular boiler houses until fully stabilized - an interim restart, not full reconstitution.

UA-CR.name: Crimea
UA-CR.status_note: Separately identified: internationally recognised as Ukraine, under Russian occupation. Not a Russian federal subject. Included in the Monitored-Area ESDI (iteration 4) through the sectors where it has qualifying events and a compatible denominator; excluded from refining/generation for lack of a base. The map does not adjudicate sovereignty through colour or polygon membership.

not_modelled.industrial_impact: No open regional industrial-consumption data ingested.
not_modelled.civilian_electricity_reliability: No outage-duration or customer-minutes-lost data source.
not_modelled.military_industrial: Out of scope: would require mapping defence production to energy supply.
not_modelled.cross_region_dependencies: Requires grid topology and inter-regional flow data not yet ingested.

refinery_reconciliation.national_estimate_source: IEA / Reuters, Russian primary refining ~6.6 mb/d (~330 MTPA)
refinery_reconciliation.note: Tracked major-refinery capacity vs the published national estimate. The gap is chiefly mini-refineries and gas-condensate plants not individually inventoried; refining exposure is measured against tracked capacity and is a lower bound. Unlike facilities are not counted merely to close the gap. Iteration 6 excluded petrochemical complexes (Tobolsk/ZapSibNeftekhim) from the fuels-refining denominator via the canonical registry.

canonical_linkage.note: Identity/linkage completeness, NOT disruption coverage: how much of the tracked denominator resolves to a struck canonical refinery. Naftan (Belarus) is intentionally outside the Russian denominator.

economic_context.provider: Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA)
economic_context.caveat: Observed external economic indicators, monthly. NOT attributed to infrastructure strikes -- export revenue moves for many reasons this data cannot separate. CREA revises historical figures as shipment data is verified; reporting month and snapshot date are preserved.

total_fossil_export_revenue.note: CREA monthly analysis. Observed economic context, not attributed to infrastructure strikes.
CREA: highest revenues in two and a half years.

crude_oil_export_revenue.note: CREA: crude oil export revenue fell 8% m/m in June 2026.

national.value_text: Reuters (via Moscow Times): as of 20 May 2026, refineries fully halted or significantly reduced after drone strikes totalled >83 Mt/yr of capacity (~238,000 t/day) -- nearly a quarter of Russia's total refining -- accounting for >30% of gasoline output and ~25% of diesel output.
Kyiv Independent (citing the Financial Times): Ukrainian strikes had hit at least 16 of Russia's 38 oil refineries since Aug 2025, pushing Russian diesel exports to their lowest level since 2020.

Moscow Times: Russia extended its gasoline export ban (exporters and producers) through 31 Dec 2025, and barred resellers from selling diesel, marine fuel and other gas oils abroad through end-2025 (direct producers exempt) -- a policy response to strike-driven domestic fuel tightness.

Moscow Times: a Kommersant estimate put the gasoline shortage at 20% (~400,000 t/month). The same article reports as observed fact that two Far East regions and annexed Crimea introduced ration cards for buying gasoline.

cur-2026-08-20-taman-500kv.value_text: After the strike on the Taman 500 kV substation, power failed around 01:45 in Simferopol, Sevastopol, Kerch, Feodosia and Yalta; Russian-installed Sevastopol authorities said restrictions were lifted after about 90 minutes, though the grid stayed unstable and some settlements remained without power. No consumer count is given.

cur-orsk-2026-08-11.value_text: Reuters: Orsknefteorgsintez ceased processing on 11 Aug after a fire from the drone attack. Nameplate ~5.76 Mt/yr (~115,200 bbl/d); in 2024 it processed 4.2 Mt of crude. (Moscow Times separately cites 6.6 Mt/yr; conflict preserved.)

Moscow Times: with the refinery fully shut, the Orenburg governor said the region would rely on fuel trucked in, and that 80% of the region's 287 filling stations were operational, priority to emergency vehicles.

Moscow Times: the Orenburg governor said repairs could take up to six months because shrapnel damaged key infrastructure hard to replace under Western sanctions. A projection, not an observed restart.

gazprom-neftekhim-salavat:2026-07-13.value_text: Meduza (industry data): the 14 July overnight strike disabled both primary crude distillation units at Salavat -- CDU-6 (17,140 t/day) and CDU-4 (11,430 t/day) -- taking the complex offline. The plant was ~2.7% of Russia's total refining throughput in 2024.

cur-2026-06-24-orenburg-gpp.value_text: World Oil: after the 24 June strike forced the Orenburg GPP to suspend intake of Karachaganak raw gas, output at Kazakhstan's Karachaganak field was cut by more than a quarter -- 34,000 t/day normally to 25,000 t/day (~180,000 bbl/d). Field oil and gas output are linked. (Interfax gives different figures; both preserved.)

Interfax (citing KazMunayGas): Karachaganak output was cut by 9,000 t/day on 26 June -- to ~28,000 from ~31,000 -- after the Orenburg plant incident, and as of 30 June was not yet fully restored. (Baseline differs from World Oil; both reported unmerged.)

cur-2025-02-03-astrakhan-gpp.value_text: Reuters (via Ukrinform): the early-Feb 2025 strike halted fuel output at Gazprom's Astrakhan GPP; the damaged gas-condensate unit has ~3 Mt/yr capacity, and industry sources said it might only resume in weeks or months. (Value is the affected unit's annual capacity; the halt is the observed effect.)

perm-refinery:2026-04-29.value_text: Reuters (via RBC-Ukraine): the CDU-4 (AVT-4) primary unit at LUKOIL's Perm refinery was out from 30 April after the 29 April strike/fire; a 7 May strike shut three more primary units and completely halted processing. The refinery ran ~12.6 Mt of crude in 2024 (~250,000 bbl/d).

syzran-refinery:2026-04-18.value_text: Hydrocarbon Processing (citing Reuters/industry): Rosneft's Syzran refinery halted processing after the 18 April attack, shutting primary unit CDU-6, which is >70% of plant capacity. Capacity 8.5 Mt/yr (~170,000 bbl/d).

volgograd-refinery:2026-06-01.value_text: Militarnyi: LUKOIL's Volgograd refinery suspended operations after the strike (this source dates it to the night of 29 May 2026 -- 2-3 days before the incident's 2026-06-01 label; likely the same event). Primary distillation unit No. 1 (~40% of capacity) stopped, as did units 5 and 6. Capacity 14.8 Mt/yr of products (~300,000 bbl/d).
